$comment: Paper-Doll Rig — closure placement contract for the 17-415 9ml Cylinder family. Verified 2026-08-01 against all five locked body plates (clear, amber, cobalt, frosted, swirl). ONE recipe seats every closure on every plate with no per-bottle tuning; that invariance IS the paper-doll architecture.

sharedNeckGeometry.$comment: Measured on all five plates. Divergence across the strip y=760..971: mean 4px, worst 12px on a single row, centerline within 3px. Below y=971 the shoulder flare diverges by up to 84px — that is real per-colorway glass, NOT a registration error, and no closure skirt may descend past it under a shared recipe.

toneContract.$comment: Bone-born plates span 34..210 luminance and clip at neither end. The harvested over-cap spans the full 0..255 with BOTH ends clipped — that foreign transfer curve, not key direction, is what reads as pasted-on. Its key highlight sits at 75% across vs 74-86% for amber/cobalt/frosted/swirl, so direction already agrees. Rung 1 of the lighting ladder is therefore sufficient here; see harmonizeToneRange() in compositeEngine.ts.

sizing.rule: flush to bodyWidthPx — the cap edge aligns with the bottle edge
sizing.$comment: NEVER size a closure off the thread crest. Doing so imports the canon-vs-photography neck discrepancy: the crest measures 269px, which at body scale (363px = 20mm, 18.15 px/mm) is 14.8mm, NOT the canon 17mm. Sizing from the crest built the cap ~13% too small twice (309px, then 345px) before Jordan called it — the body is the trustworthy scale.

sizing.rule: flush to threadCrestPx — the roller housing seats INSIDE the neck bore
